comments.note: ThumbnailsView.axaml ListBoxItem.IsSelected sync uses {ReflectionBinding} in the Style setter. In Avalonia 11, Styles cannot carry x:DataType, so the compiled binding resolver falls back to using the UserControl's DataContext type (ThumbnailsViewModel), causing AVLN2000. ReflectionBinding is the documented Avalonia escape hatch for this scenario and is well-understood, but it means one setter per item goes through reflection. This is the same approach used project-wide for ListBox item-selection sync.

ThumbnailsViewModel.DeleteSelected iterates and removes items one-by-one from the ObservableCollection. Each removal fires a CollectionChanged notification. For large thumbnail collections (e.g., 50+ items being deleted simultaneously), a batch remove approach (iterate in reverse by index, or rebuild after deletion) would reduce UI thrash. Acceptable for typical use but worth noting for M10.

ThumbnailsViewModel fire-and-forget bitmap loads (`_ = item.LoadBitmapAsync(_cts.Token)`) use _cts (the dispose token), not a load-specific token. Triggering a second LoadCommand before the first load finishes does not cancel the in-flight bitmap loads from the first load; old items are disposed via Thumbnails.Clear() but their bitmap tasks continue running until _cts is cancelled (i.e., Dispose). This is benign — setting Bitmap on a disposed item is safe — but a per-load CancellationTokenSource would be cleaner.

IThumbnailViewerService was created as an App-layer interface (src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/) rather than in Core/Abstractions, consistent with the existing IDialogService and other Avalonia-specific service contracts in the App project. This is the correct layer per constraints.md.

summary: Reviewed IThumbnailViewerService.cs, ThumbnailsViewModel.cs, ThumbnailsView.axaml, and ThumbnailsView.axaml.cs against all four Review Dimensions.

Maintainability: Well-structured ViewModel. Per-item PropertyChanged subscription/unsubscription in OnThumbnailsCollectionChanged is the correct pattern for tracking collection item state. Dispose() is comprehensive (cancel _cts, dispose _cts, unsubscribe CollectionChanged, unsubscribe all item handlers, dispose all items, clear). IThumbnailViewerService is a clean interface stub.

Best Practices: CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource correctly combines the command token and the ViewModel's own _cts.Token. ReflectionBinding in ListBoxItem Style is documented with an explanatory comment. JumpToPosition stub with CanExecute always returning false is the correct M10 deferral pattern. x:DataType compiled bindings used throughout.

Fix-Forward applied: Load() now explicitly unsubscribes item.PropertyChanged -= OnItemPropertyChanged before item.Dispose() in the pre-clear loop, matching the pattern already used in Dispose(). This prevents silent subscription leaks when Thumbnails.Clear() fires a Reset event with no OldItems.
Architecture: IThumbnailViewerService correctly placed in App.Services (not Core) as a UI-hosting concern. The interface stub breaks the WP-019/WP-021 dependency cycle cleanly.

comments.note: reviewer-applied-fix: In ThumbnailsViewModel.Load(), added explicit `item.PropertyChanged -= OnItemPropertyChanged` before `item.Dispose()` in the pre-clear loop. Thumbnails.Clear() fires a Reset CollectionChanged event with OldItems=null, so the OnThumbnailsCollectionChanged handler skips the unsubscription loop. Without the explicit unsubscribe, old items retain a live delegate to the ViewModel. GC can still collect them (no strong root holds the old items), but the explicit unsubscribe is cleaner and makes the Load() pattern consistent with Dispose().

ThumbnailsView.axaml ReflectionBinding in ListBoxItem Style is documented with a comment explaining the Avalonia 11 limitation. Context menu #Root.((vm:ThumbnailsViewModel)DataContext) element-reference bindings are the idiomatic Avalonia approach for DataTemplate items needing parent commands. Both patterns are correct and consistent with the codebase.
